subject: ACME renewal & expansion recap / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>, Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: ACME renewal & expansion recap / next steps

Hi Jordan & Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really productive conversation. Quick recap of what we covered and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of usage & ask:
- Current footprint: ~18M tokens/day across chat & batch generation; embeddings volume has grown ~2.5x in the last quarter.
- Primary goals: reduce per-token cost for embeddings, stabilize 99th percentile latency during peak (2–4pm PT), and scope private deployment options for PII-heavy workloads.

Pain points you highlighted:
- Latency spikes on long-context chat sessions during peak hours.
- Embedding compute is driving up monthly spend and unpredictable billing for experiments.
- Legal/regulatory team needs clarity on data isolation options for the new summarization pipeline.

Proposed expansion path & timeline:
1) Increase committed Dedicated capacity for embeddings (add 2x dedicated nodes) — reduces per-embed unit cost by ~28%.
2) Pilot private VPC for the summarization workflow (month-long pilot, can be scoped as on-prem/VPC).
3) Add real-time chat routing optimization (KV cache tuning + batching tweaks) to address latency spikes.

Suggested next steps:
- I’ll send an updated proposal and SOW with pricing scenarios (attached) by tomorrow (Sep 13).
- Jordan / procurement to confirm internal approval timeline by Sep 19 so we can finalize discounts and sign by Oct 1.
- Schedule a 30-min procurement/legal call w/ your team — proposed window Sep 20–22.

Attachments included: ACME_Renewal_Proposal_20270912.pdf, ACME_SOW_Q4_2027.docx, pricing breakdown spreadsheet.

If I missed anything or you want changes to the scope, flag them and I’ll update. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk the SOW.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: ACME_Renewal_Proposal_20270912.pdf (PDF, 6 pages) | ACME_SOW_Q4_2027.docx (Word, 4 pages) | ACME_pricing_breakdown.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME renewal & expansion recap / next steps

Thanks Marissa — quick confirmation and a couple of clarifications.

On Sep 12, 2027, at 1:02 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> - Current footprint: ~18M tokens/day across chat & batch generation; embeddings volume has grown ~2.5x in the last quarter.
> - Primary goals: reduce per-token cost for embeddings, stabilize 99th percentile latency during peak (2–4pm PT), and scope private deployment options for PII-heavy workloads.

All accurate. Two clarifications: 
1) The embeddings growth number is closer to 2.2x vs 2.5x (we reconciled instrumenting differences).
2) For the pilot, legal will only approve a VPC-managed option (not fully on-prem) unless we present additional audit controls.

We are very interested in the Dedicated capacity option — that looks like the fastest way to impact our costs. Please include a TCO-style comparison (current spend vs committed + discount) in the updated pricing worksheet.

Also looping procurement (procurement@acme.com) — Samantha, can your team confirm internal approval window? We’re aiming to get the contract signed before Oct 1 to avoid pricing changes in Q4.

Appreciate the follow up — looking forward to the updated docs.

—Jordan
Director of ML Platforms, ACME Corp
jordan.ellis@acme.com

---
Quoted for context; let me know if you want the raw logs from our cost analytics as well.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>, Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Updated proposal & SOW (attachments) — includes TCO scenarios

Jordan / Samantha,

Attached is an updated proposal that reflects the 2.2x embeddings growth you called out and the VPC-only pilot constraint. Highlights: 
- Pricing: committed Dedicated capacity (2x nodes) with a stepped discount structure — 20% off list for a 12-month commit, 25% with a 24-month commit.
- TCO sheet compares your current monthly run-rate vs expected monthly after commit (attached spreadsheet). Short summary: estimated ~26% reduction in per-embed cost under the 12-month commit, ~33% under 24-month.
- Pilot scope: 4-week VPC-managed pilot for the summarization pipeline (includes network isolation, KMS integration, and audit logs).

Attachments: ACME_Renewal_Proposal_20270913.pdf (updated), ACME_SOW_Q4_2027.docx, ACME_pricing_breakdown.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement/Legal call — please suggest availability Sep 20–22 (30 minutes).
2) Finalize discount level and commit length by Sep 23 so we can route for internal approvals.
3) Target DocuSign send by Sep 27 and sign by Oct 1.

Ben, looping you for visibility on the discount band and to confirm capacity availability for a Nov pilot start.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the TCO if that helps.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samantha Holt <procurement@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME renewal & expansion recap / next steps

Marissa / Jordan — thanks for the summary and updated materials. Procurement confirms we can target an internal approval window that ends Sep 23. A few notes: 

- We’ll need the final pricing table (showing list vs committed pricing and the exact discount) and the SOW with pilot acceptance criteria by EOD Sep 16 so we can circulate to Legal.
- DocuSign is fine; please include a single master SOW and a one-page pricing exhibit.
- If you can provide the run-rate comparison (current vs committed) as a one-pager, that will speed the review.

Assuming those items are in place we’ll push to sign before Oct 1. I’ll schedule a 30-min slot for Sep 21 for procurement/legal review and invite the necessary stakeholders.

Thanks — Samantha Holt
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Corp
procurement@acme.com

---
Procurement accepted items to follow: final pricing exhibit, one-page run-rate comparison, signed SOW via DocuSign
